key_insight: Polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation reveals hidden, giant circular dichroism in chiral 2D halide perovskites, enabling telecom-band chiral light detection with opposite-handed responses in orthogonal channels.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new route to compact, wavelength-relevant chiral photodetectors and optical security devices for telecom photonics, encryption, and anti-counterfeiting.
method: Use chiral 2D perovskite (R/S-MBACl)2PbI4 as the nonlinear optical medium.
Measure third-harmonic generation circular dichroism with polarization-resolved detection.
Separate orthogonal THG polarization channels to uncover hidden chiral anisotropy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exceptionally large dissymmetry factors exceeding 1.9 when the hidden polarization-dependent contributions are separated, versus underestimation in conventional total-THG measurements.
watch_item: Performance claims depend on polarization-resolved readout, so device design must preserve polarization selectivity and avoid averaging that masks the true chiral response.
paper_title: Telecom-band Chiral Light Detection through Hidden Giant Third-Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Two-dimensional Halide Perovskite
